selector.rationale: The patient's presentation of discrete, dark red, circular lesions in the axilla with severe pruritus and the biopsy findings of lymphocytes obscuring the dermal-epidermal junction are most consistent with inverse lichen planus, which is a subtype of lichen planus that typically affects the skin folds.

rejected.label: Granuloma annulare
rejected.why: Lack of characteristic biopsy findings of granulomatous inflammation

rejected.label: Dermatitis Herpetiformis
rejected.why: Absence of blisters and lack of response to discontinuation of underarm deodorant

rejected.label: Mycosis Fungoides
rejected.why: Lack of characteristic biopsy findings of atypical lymphocytes

rejected.label: contact dermatitis
rejected.why: Lack of response to discontinuation of underarm deodorant and no clear environmental trigger

rejected.label: Lichen planus
rejected.why: While lichen planus is a possible diagnosis, the presentation is more consistent with inverse lichen planus due to the location and morphology of the lesions
